media.description: Cabin-class Salon de Thé aboard the French Line S.S. Champlain while associated with Pier 57 on the North River in 1932. The photograph documents the passenger-liner setting connected with the historical pier; it does not show the pier building or establish Kaper’s presence.

timelineEvents.title: Arrival in New York en route to Los Angeles
timelineEvents.label: 24 Oct 1934 · Arrival in New York
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper arrived in New York from France with Eleonora on a temporary visa, travelling onward to Los Angeles.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Kaper and his wife Eleonora sailed from Le Havre on 17 October 1934 aboard the S.S. Champlain in second cabin class and reached New York on 24 October. Their non-immigrant visas had been issued in Paris on 15 October, numbered in a single series with the Jurmanns’ (NI 1581–1584), and the manifest records Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer as having paid the passage and as the party they were joining in Culver City. Kaper gave his occupation as musician and declared that he meant to stay about eight months and then return, without seeking United States citizenship. David Blum of the Culver Export Corporation met them in New York, and they left for Hollywood on 27 October.

places.authorizedName: French Line Pier 57, North River, foot of West 15th Street, Manhattan, New York
places.publicNote: Approximate arrival site for Kaper and Eleonora’s 1934 Atlantic crossing from Le Havre aboard the S.S. Champlain. In this period the French Line (Compagnie Générale Transatlantique) used Pier 57 on the North River, at the foot of West 15th Street; the pier is inferred from the line’s documented berth rather than named in the passenger manifest. The record establishes arrival at New York but not processing at Ellis Island.
